summary.headline: Capri Global Q4 FY26 PAT hit record INR283 crore (+59% YoY) and FY26 PAT INR949 crore (~2x), with consolidated gross Stage 3 down to 0.9%.
summary.overview: Capri Global posted its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR283 crore in Q4 FY26, up 59% YoY, with FY26 PAT of INR949 crore, almost double the prior year. Consolidated AUM reached INR36,623 crore (+60% YoY, +20% QoQ), led by gold loans at INR16,965 crore (+111% YoY, +33% QoQ). Asset quality improved, with consolidated gross Stage 3 at 0.9% (down 61 bps QoQ) and net Stage 3 at 0.5%. Management reiterated FY28 targets of INR55,000 crore AUM (revised FY28 AUM guidance cited as INR57,000 crore in Q&A, with FY27 at INR46,000 crore), ROA 4-4.5% and ROE 16-18%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR16,965 crore (+111% YoY, +33% QoQ), about 46% of AUM. Gross Stage 3 at 0.3%. Branch AUM INR17 crore vs INR14 crore last quarter; 90% of branches above INR5 crore breakeven. Co-lending share in gold fell to about 31% from about 39%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,465 crore (+23% YoY); FY26 disbursement INR2,550 crore (+65% YoY). Micro-LAP AUM INR824 crore. Gross Stage 3 flat at 3%.

segments.name: Housing finance (CGHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR7,447 crore (+43% YoY). Self-employed share 74% of AUM. Gross Stage 3 at 1%, improved QoQ. 25 branches in South India.

segments.name: Construction finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR5,708 crore (+38% YoY) across 282 active projects; average sanction ticket INR48 crore. Gross Stage 3 at 0.3%; Stage 2 reduced by INR53 crore on collections and rollback of 3 accounts.

segments.name: Co-lending and DA
segments.commentary: Co-lending AUM INR7,783 crore (+91% YoY, 21% of AUM). Co-lending and DA income INR97 crore (+76% YoY, -16% QoQ). New RBI co-lending norms from 1 Jan 2026 are causing a temporary slowdown.

segments.name: Insurance distribution and car loan distribution
segments.commentary: Insurance net fee income INR65 crore in Q4 and INR153 crore in FY26. Car loan origination INR3,492 crore in Q4 (+18% YoY) and INR11,910 crore in FY26 (+13% YoY), across 14 partner banks and FIs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance about INR1,300 crore (per Q&A).
FY27 AUM guidance INR46,000 crore; FY28 AUM about INR57,000 crore (raised about INR2,000 crore), with conservative 25% overall growth assumed. Opening remarks reiterated INR55,000 crore AUM by FY28.
FY27 ROA about 4% and ROE not less than 16%; medium-term FY28 ROA 4-4.5% and ROE 16-18%.
Cost of borrowing: about 10-20 bps reduction in FY27 (management cited ~9% exit cost, 'conservatively 9%'); a further ~20 bps possible after an expected credit rating upgrade within 6-9 months.
Sustainable credit cost about 0.7% of average total assets (historical range 0.6-0.7%). Co-lending and DA about 20% of total AUM. Gold mix may reach about 50%.
Branch additions of about 700-800 over two years, including about 350 gold loan branches in FY27 to be operational within the year. No RBI permission now needed.

Fee guidance: car loan income +12-15%, insurance income +25-30%, co-lending income flat; capital markets/bond vertical net fee income INR20-25 crore (gross INR40-50 crore) once licence (expected by end-June) is obtained.
capex_capacity: Net addition of 98 branches in Q4 FY26 and 318 in FY26, taking the network to 1,429 locations; 89 gold branches added in Q4 (36 Telangana, 18 Andhra Pradesh, 8 Karnataka, 20 Odisha).
Plan of about 700-800 branches over two years, mainly gold loan; about 350 gold loan branches this fiscal year.
Employee base up 5% QoQ (692 net additions); gold loan AUM per employee INR3.1 crore vs INR1.6 crore earlier.
Tier 2 capital may be raised; DA and co-lending expected to conserve capital over 18-24 months. CGCL standalone CRAR fell to 25.8%, driven by subsidiary investments.
Proposed international bond issuance deferred for 2-4 months due to higher hedging costs linked to the West Asia situation; ratings from Fitch (BB, stable) and Moody's (Ba3 CFR, stable) obtained.
demand_pricing: Gold loan yields fell sequentially by about 90 bps; management attributed this to co-lending gold loans at lower yields, which it said are accretive to profit per branch. Gold portfolio LTV about 66%; new disbursement LTV about 70%.

Co-lending rules (effective 1 Jan 2026) require interest accrued in LTV on moratorium loans and income assessment above INR2.5 lakh. Partners expected to go live by June, with full volumes from the September quarter.
No deterioration seen in MSME collection efficiency or asset quality from recent macro events.
Car loan distribution to add used cars this year, then credit cards, personal loans and mortgages over 3-4 years; target of about INR60-70 crore fee income over 4-5 years.
Housing yields rising as the self-employed mix increased to 74%.

qa_highlights.question: Target gold loan mix and branch plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold mix can reach about 50% from about 46%. About 700-800 branches over two years, including about 350 gold branches in FY27; no RBI permission needed.

qa_highlights.question: Gold yield sustainability and co-lending target?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower gold yields reflect co-lending and volume growth, which management says is accretive. Combined co-lending and DA target is about 20% of total AUM.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Expect 10-20 bps reduction in FY27, with exit around 9%. A further 20 bps is possible after a rating upgrade expected within 6-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About 0.7% for the year; Q4 0.8% included a INR16 crore macro management overlay. No slippage seen; most provisions are on new book.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 PAT and AUM guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PAT guidance about INR1,300 crore. AUM guidance INR46,000 crore for FY27 and about INR57,000 crore for FY28 (25% conservative growth).

qa_highlights.question: Gold LTV risk if prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin call to restore LTV within 75%, then 14-day notice and auction if not met. Portfolio LTV about 66%.

risks_watch: Co-lending volumes likely to slow for one to two quarters under new RBI norms; full volume expected from the September 2026 quarter.
Gold price volatility with a 70% new-disbursement LTV; a sharp fall would trigger margin calls or auctions.
Gold yield compression (about 90 bps QoQ), with branch-level profitability depending on continued volume growth.
Cost of funds guidance depends on a rating upgrade and on rate moves after elections; international bond timing depends on hedging costs.
Capital adequacy: CGCL standalone CRAR fell to 25.8%; capital plan relies on DA, co-lending and possible Tier 2 issuance.
Q4 PCR of 41.2% and credit cost of 0.8% including overlay; watch whether the management overlay reverses.
key_quotes: With this backdrop, I am pleased to say that Capri Global has delivered strong quarterly performance in Q4 FY '26, continuing its growth momentum and maintaining asset quality while delivering highest ever quarterly profit of INR283 crores, a 59% increase year -on-year and full year profit of INR949 crores, almost double from the last year.
So overall, if you look at our business mix is designed in a manner to grow in tandem with the overall growth.
So, portfolio level LTV is about 66%. And on the new disbursement, LTV is about 70%.
So overall growth, we are targeting conservatively 25%. And we are giving a guidance of INR46,000 crores by end of FY '27 and about INR57,000 crores by FY '28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, profitability and asset quality, citing record Q4 PAT, Stage 3 at 0.9% and reiterated FY28 targets. Cautious on near-term co-lending volumes under new RBI norms, cost of funds (guided only 10-20 bps FY27 reduction), gold price risk and international bond timing; several answers hedged with "depends on" and "conservatively".

growth.why: Management guides FY27 AUM of INR46,000 crore and FY27 PAT about INR1,300 crore (vs FY26 PAT INR949 crore), backed by ~350 gold branches due within FY27 and a 33% QoQ gold AUM rise, though no explicit AUM capex or order numbers were given beyond branch counts.
